'''Maryna Sergiivna Viazovska''' ({{langx|uk|Марина Сергіївна Вязовська}},<ref name="VNLU">{{citation|url=http://www.irbis-nbuv.gov.ua/cgi-bin/irbis_nbuv/cgiirbis_64.exe?Z21ID=&I21DBN=ARD&P21DBN=ARD&S21STN=1&S21REF=10&S21FMT=fullwebr&C21COM=S&S21CNR=20&S21P01=0&S21P02=0&S21P03=A=&S21COLORTERMS=1&S21STR=Вязовська%20М.С.$|language=Ukrainian|title=Вязовська М.С.|work=Catalogues|publisher=[[Vernadsky National Library of Ukraine]]|access-date=6 April 2016|archive-date=2 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140802001656/http://www.irbis-nbuv.gov.ua/cgi-bin/irbis_nbuv/cgiirbis_64.exe?Z21ID=|url-status=live}}</ref> {{IPA|uk|mɐˈrɪnɐ wʲɐˈzɔu̯sʲkɐ|pron}}; born 2 December 1984<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.deutsche-digitale-bibliothek.de/entity/1046435000|title=Maryna Viazovska|language=German|publisher=[[German National Library]]|access-date=7 April 2016|archive-date=30 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180730170914/https://www.deutsche-digitale-bibliothek.de/entity/1046435000|url-status=live}}</ref>) is a Ukrainian mathematician known for her work in [[sphere packing]]. She is a full professor and Chair of [[Number Theory]] at the Institute of Mathematics of the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] in Switzerland.<ref name=":0" /> She was awarded the [[Fields Medal]] in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fields Medals 2022 |url=https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-2022 |access-date=5 July 2022 |website=International Mathematical Union |archive-date=5 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220705072608/https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-2022 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=qf>{{cite web|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/ukrainian-mathematician-maryna-viazovska-wins-fields-medal-20220705/|title=In Times of Scarcity, War and Peace, a Ukrainian Finds the Magic in Math|first1=Thomas|last1=Lin|first2=Erica|last2=Klarreich|publisher=[[Quanta Magazine]]|website=quantamagazine.org|date=5 July 2022|accessdate=5 July 2022|archive-date=5 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220705072102/https://www.quantamagazine.org/ukrainian-mathematician-maryna-viazovska-wins-fields-medal-20220705/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Viazovska was born in [[Kyiv]], the oldest of three sisters. Her father was a chemist who worked at the [[Antonov]] aircraft factory, and her mother was an [[engineer]].<ref name=qf/> She attended a specialized secondary school for high-achieving students in science and technology, [[Kyiv Natural Science Lyceum No. 145]]. An influential teacher there, Andrii Knyazyuk, had previously worked as a professional research mathematician before becoming a secondary school teacher.<ref name=mactutor>{{MacTutor|id=Viazovska}}</ref> Viazovska competed in domestic mathematics Olympiads when she was at high school, placing 13th in a national competition where 12 students were selected to a training camp before a six-member team for the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] was chosen.<ref name=qf/> As a student at [[Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv]], she competed at the [[International Mathematics Competition for University Students]] in 2002, 2003, 2004, and 2005, and was one of the first-place winners in 2002 and 2005.<ref>IMC official results: [http://www.imc-math.org.uk/index.php?year=2002&item=results 2002] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191028215315/http://www.imc-math.org.uk/index.php?year=2002&item=results |date=28 October 2019 }}, [http://www.imc-math.org.uk/imc2003/results2003.html 2003] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201123111505/https://www.imc-math.org.uk/imc2003/results2003.html |date=23 November 2020 }}, [http://www.imc-math.org.uk/imc2004/results2004.html 2004] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021082207/https://imc-math.org.uk/imc2004/results2004.html |date=21 October 2020 }}, and [http://www.imc-math.org.uk/imc2005/results2005.html 2005] . Retrieved 7 April 2016.</ref> She co-authored her first research paper in 2005.<ref name=qf/>

Viazovska earned a master's from the [[University of Kaiserslautern]] in 2007, [[Candidate of Sciences|PhD]] from the [[Institute of Mathematics of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]] in 2010,<ref name="VNLU" /> and a doctorate ([[Dr. rer. nat.]]) from the [[University of Bonn]] in 2013. Her doctoral dissertation, ''Modular Functions and Special Cycles'', concerns [[analytic number theory]] and was supervised by [[Don Zagier]] and [[Werner Müller (mathematician)|Werner Müller]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://bonndoc.ulb.uni-bonn.de/xmlui/handle/20.500.11811/5795|year=2013|title=Modular Functions and Special Cycles|publisher=[[University of Bonn]]|first=Maryna|last=Viazovska|series=Doctoral dissertation|access-date=1 April 2016|archive-date=13 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170613021238/http://hss.ulb.uni-bonn.de/2013/3415/3415.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>

She was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Berlin Mathematical School]] and the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]]<ref name="quanta"/> and a Minerva Distinguished Visitor<ref>[https://www.math.princeton.edu/events/seminars/minerva-mini-course/archive/11 Minerva Distinguished Visitor Lectures] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200322134712/https://www.math.princeton.edu/events/seminars/minerva-mini-course/archive/11 |date=22 March 2020 }}, Princeton University, retrieved 14 June 2020.</ref> at [[Princeton University]]. Since January 2018 she has held the Chair of Number Theory as a [[full professor]] at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] (EPFL) in Switzerland after a short stint as [[Academic tenure|tenure-track]] assistant professor.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/maryna-viazovska-promoted-to-full-professor/|title=Maryna Viazovska promoted to Full Professor|first=Andrea|last=Testa|date=1 August 2018|via=actu.epfl.ch|access-date=9 January 2018|archive-date=30 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191030164627/https://actu.epfl.ch/news/maryna-viazovska-promoted-to-full-professor/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Contributions==
In 2016, Viazovska solved the [[sphere packing|sphere-packing problem]] in [[dimension]]&nbsp;8.<ref>{{citation|title=Stacking Cannonballs In 8 Dimensions|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/kevinknudson/2016/03/29/stacking-cannonballs-in-8-dimensions/|magazine=[[Forbes]]|first=Kevin|last=Knudson|date=29 March 2016|access-date=4 September 2017|archive-date=30 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180730172730/https://www.forbes.com/sites/kevinknudson/2016/03/29/stacking-cannonballs-in-8-dimensions/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{citation|last1=Morgan|first1=Frank|authorlink=Frank Morgan (mathematician)|title=Sphere Packing in Dimension 8|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/frank-morgan/sphere-packing-in-dimensi_b_9496736.html|date=21 March 2016|newspaper=[[The Huffington Post]]|access-date=31 March 2016|archive-date=11 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170211051427/http://www.huffingtonpost.com/frank-morgan/sphere-packing-in-dimensi_b_9496736.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{citation|url=http://www.zeit.de/wissen/2016-03/mathematik-kugeln-dicht-packen-achte-dimension|title=So stapeln Mathematiker Melonen|language=German|first=Andreas|last=Loos|date=21 March 2016|newspaper=[[Die Zeit]]|access-date=1 April 2016|archive-date=30 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180730204119/https://www.zeit.de/wissen/2016-03/mathematik-kugeln-dicht-packen-achte-dimension|url-status=live}}</ref> Her dimension 8 solution quickly led to collaboration with others, and a solution in dimension&nbsp;24.<ref name="newscientist">{{citation|last1=Grossman|first1=Lisa|title=New maths proof shows how to stack oranges in 24 dimensions|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/2082328-new-maths-proof-shows-how-to-stack-oranges-in-24-dimensions/|date=28 March 2016|magazine=[[New Scientist]]|department=Daily News|access-date=31 March 2016|archive-date=30 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180730170823/https://www.newscientist.com/article/2082328-new-maths-proof-shows-how-to-stack-oranges-in-24-dimensions/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="quanta">{{citation|last1=Klarreich|first1=Erica|authorlink1=Erica Klarreich|title=Sphere Packing Solved in Higher Dimensions|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/20160330-sphere-packing-solved-in-higher-dimensions|magazine=Quanta Magazine|date=30 March 2016|access-date=31 March 2016|archive-date=12 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170312181737/https://www.quantamagazine.org/20160330-sphere-packing-solved-in-higher-dimensions/|url-status=live}}</ref> Previously, the problem had been solved only for three or fewer dimensions, and the proof of the three-dimensional version (the [[Kepler conjecture]]) involved long computer calculations. In contrast, Viazovska's proof for 8 and 24 dimensions has been described as "stunningly simple".<ref name="quanta"/>

A few years later, in 2018, Viazovska and her collaborators significantly extended<ref name="UniversalOptimality">{{cite journal | last1=Cohn | first1=Henry | last2=Kumar | first2=Abhinav | last3=Miller | first3=Stephen | last4=Radchenko | first4=Danylo | last5=Viazovska | first5=Maryna | title=Universal optimality of the $E_8$ and Leech lattices and interpolation formulas | journal=Annals of Mathematics | volume=196 | issue=3 | date=1 November 2022 | issn=0003-486X | doi=10.4007/annals.2022.196.3.3 | doi-access=free | pages=983–1082| arxiv=1902.05438 }}</ref> their sphere packing results in dimensions 8 and 24 to address potential energy minimization.<ref>{{Cite web |title="Science is a soft power." Maryna Viazovska, the face of Ukrainian mathematics |url=https://www.weareukraine.info/special/science-is-a-soft-power-maryna-viazovska-the-face-of-ukrainian-mathematics/ |access-date=2025-03-19 |website=We Are Ukraine |language=uk}}</ref> In 2019, Viazovska and her team solved a mathematical equation that determines how an infinite number of points repelling each other are placed in 8- and 24-dimensional spaces.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ukrinform.ua/rubric-culture/2699941-ukrainska-vcena-zdijsnila-proriv-u-matematici.html|title=Українська вчена здійснила прорив у математиці|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190514160532/https://www.ukrinform.ua/rubric-culture/2699941-ukrainska-vcena-zdijsnila-proriv-u-matematici.html|archive-date=2019-05-14|work=Укрінформ|date=2019-05-14|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="q19">{{cite news|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/universal-math-solutions-in-dimensions-8-and-24-20190513/|title=Out of a Magic Math Function, One Solution to Rule Them All|first=Erica|last=Klarreich|date=2019-05-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190513153115/https://www.quantamagazine.org/universal-math-solutions-in-dimensions-8-and-24-20190513/|archive-date=2019-05-13|url-status=live|language=en}}</ref><ref name="siaz">[https://www.nas.gov.ua/siaz/Ways_of_development_of_Ukrainian_science/Issues1/1604.04.pdf Український математик розв’язала столітню математичну проблему / Як упакувати кулі. Робота українського математика стала світовою сенсацією] // Шляхи розвитку української науки № 4 (125) квітень 2016, стор. 69-71 / Інформаційно-аналітичний бюлетень. Додаток до журналу «Україна: події, факти, коментарі»</ref>

As well as for her work on sphere packing, Viazovska is also known for her research on [[spherical design]]s with Bondarenko and Radchenko. With them she proved a conjecture of [[Jacob Korevaar|Korevaar]] and Meyers on the existence of small designs in arbitrary dimensions. This result was one of the contributions for which her co-author Andriy Bondarenko won the Vasil A. Popov Prize for [[approximation theory]] in 2013.<ref>{{citation|url=http://imi.cas.sc.edu/popov-prize-previous-winners/#2013|title=Popov Prize previous winners|publisher=University of South Carolina, Interdisciplinary Mathematics Institute|access-date=2 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151031043701/http://imi.cas.sc.edu/popov-prize-previous-winners/#2013|archive-date=31 October 2015|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2016, Viazovska received the [[Salem Prize]]<ref>{{citation|url=http://smf.emath.fr/content/prix-salem-2016|title=Prix Salem 2016|publisher=Société Mathématique de France|language=fr|access-date=26 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170704221107/http://smf.emath.fr/content/prix-salem-2016|archive-date=4 July 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> and, in 2017, the [[Clay Research Award]] and the [[SASTRA Ramanujan Prize]] for her work on sphere packing and [[modular form]]s.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.claymath.org/events/news/2017-clay-research-awards|title=2017 Clay Research Awards|publisher=Clay Mathematics Institute|language=en|access-date=26 September 2017|archive-date=11 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180111180359/http://www.claymath.org/events/news/2017-clay-research-awards|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{citation|url=http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-tamilnadu/maryna-viazovska-to-receive-2017-sastra-ramanujan-prize/article19754956.ece|title=Maryna Viazovska to receive 2017 SASTRA Ramanujan Prize|date=26 September 2017|newspaper=The Hindu|access-date=26 September 2017|language=en-IN|issn=0971-751X|archive-date=17 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190217184205/https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-tamilnadu/maryna-viazovska-to-receive-2017-sastra-ramanujan-prize/article19754956.ece|url-status=live}}</ref> In December 2017, she was awarded a 2018 [[New Horizons Prize in Mathematics]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/3/L3820|title=Breakthrough Prize – Mathematics Laureates – Maryna Viazovska|website=breakthroughprize.org|language=en|access-date=4 December 2017|quote=For remarkable application of the theory of modular forms to the sphere packing problem in special dimensions.|archive-date=27 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180827044035/https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/3/L3820|url-status=live}}</ref>
She was an invited speaker at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].<ref name=icm>{{citation|url=http://www.icm2018.org/portal/en/invited-section-lectures-speakers|title=Invited section lectures|work=ICM 2018|access-date=8 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181208144537/http://www.icm2018.org/portal/en/invited-section-lectures-speakers|archive-date=8 December 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> For 2019 she was awarded the [[Ruth Lyttle Satter Prize in Mathematics]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=4761|title=News from the AMS|website=American Mathematical Society|access-date=28 April 2021|archive-date=7 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107075650/https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=4761|url-status=live}}</ref> and the [[Fermat Prize]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/spip.php?article950&lang=fr|title=Institut de Mathématiques de Toulouse – Prix Fermat 2019|website=www.math.univ-toulouse.fr|access-date=12 December 2019|archive-date=1 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200701235641/https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/spip.php?article950&lang=fr|url-status=live}}</ref> She is one of the 2020 winners of the [[EMS Prize]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/news/20/05/8/prize-winners-announced|title=Prize Winners Announced|publisher=European Mathematical Society|date=8 May 2020|access-date=8 May 2020|archive-date=25 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925105323/https://euro-math-soc.eu/news/20/05/8/prize-winners-announced|url-status=live}}</ref>  In 2020, she also received the National Latsis Prize awarded by the [[Latsis Foundation]].<ref>{{citation|title=National Latsis Prize – SNF|url=http://www.snf.ch/en/theSNSF/awards/national-latsis-prize/Pages/default.aspx|access-date=21 September 2020|website=www.snf.ch|archive-date=25 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925014526/http://www.snf.ch/en/theSNSF/awards/national-latsis-prize/Pages/default.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref> She was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2021.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Viazovska_Maryna|title=Maryna Viazovska|work=Members|publisher=Academia Europaea|access-date=12 March 2022|archive-date=12 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220312185347/https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Viazovska_Maryna|url-status=live}}</ref> She was appointed Senior Scholar at the [[Clay Mathematics Institute]] in July 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Maryna Viazovska {{!}} Clay Mathematics Institute |url=https://www.claymath.org/people/maryna-viazovska-0 |access-date=28 May 2022 |website=www.claymath.org |archive-date=3 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220603070037/https://www.claymath.org/people/maryna-viazovska-0 |url-status=live }}</ref>

She was awarded the [[Fields Medal]] in July 2022, making her the second woman (after [[Maryam Mirzakhani]]), the second person born in the [[Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic|Ukrainian SSR]] (after [[Vladimir Drinfeld]]) and the first with a degree from a Ukrainian university to ever receive it.<ref name="Cohn Viazovska ">{{cite arXiv | last=Cohn | first=Henry | title=The work of Maryna Viazovska | year=2022 | eprint=2207.06913 | page=| class=math.MG }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-society/3522571-ukrainian-viazovska-wins-fields-medal-2022.html|title=Ukrainian Viazovska wins Fields Medal 2022|website=www.ukrinform.net|date=5 July 2022 |access-date=5 July 2022|archive-date=7 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220707010822/https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-society/3522571-ukrainian-viazovska-wins-fields-medal-2022.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal|title=Fields Medal &#124; International Mathematical Union (IMU)|access-date=5 July 2022|archive-date=26 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181226015744/https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal|url-status=live}}</ref> She was honored as one of the [[100 Women (BBC)|BBC 100 Women]] in December 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BBC 100 Women 2022: Who is on the list this year? |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/resources/idt-75af095e-21f7-41b0-9c5f-a96a5e0615c1 |access-date=2022-12-10 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Viazovska met her husband, Daniil Evtushinsky, at an after-school physics group for schoolchildren. He is also a researcher at EPFL, in physics. They have two children, a son and a daughter.<ref name="qf"/><ref name="allnews">{{cite web |last=Daniel |first=Jonny |date=5 July 2022 |title=Mathematics: Fields Medal for Maryna Viazovska |work=All News Press |url=https://allnewspress.com/mathematics-fields-medal-for-maryna-viazovska-knowledge/ |access-date=7 July 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220708041635/https://allnewspress.com/mathematics-fields-medal-for-maryna-viazovska-knowledge/ |archive-date=8 July 2022}}</ref>
